text:
alex: Heads up — CI applied a change to the apac GPU pool and then the GH Action runner got cancelled mid-apply. Terraform reported a lock but the apply never finished, now the apac pool is in a half-provisioned state. Anyone see the same?
priya: ugh, saw alerts about failed node registration and partial ASG size increase. Are we still holding the Dynamo lock?
sam: I can confirm dynamo lock key exists and lease TTL shows expired in CloudWatch but the lock item hasn't been deleted. Looks like our lock cleanup path didn't run because the runner was SIGKILL.
marta: is this the cross-account state replication job we enabled last month (s3 replication to apac-account)? could replication lag cause the state mismatch during apply?
alex: yes — state backend is in us-west with cross-account s3 replication to apac-account for DR. My hunch: runner cancelled after it uploaded a partial state move, dynamo got a new lock with provider v1.8 format, but our lock-cleaner expects v1.7 key shape. result: orphaned lock and a replicated state file that diverges.
priya: do we have a safe unlock procedure? don't want two concurrent applies touching the gpu autoscaling group and ending up +N GPUs (cost shock).
terraform-bot: NOTE: remote state lock detected: table=infra-tf-locks, key=apac/gpu-pool. Holder=gha-runner-5623, ttl=0 (expired).
ci-bot: Reproduction: cancel GH Action step during terraform apply -> dynamo item remains, lock owner differs across provider versions.
sam: manual unlock steps I did previously: 1) terraform state pull > save locally, 2) verify last remote object, 3) run `aws dynamodb delete-item` on the lock key, 4) re-run `terraform plan` against pulled state. But that is manual and risky if replication lag exists.
alex: let's avoid manual delete if replication hasn't caught up. plan: 1) pause any CI applies to apac (set flag in ci-config), 2) run `aws s3api head-object` on replicated state in apac-account and compare etag to primary, 3) only delete dynamo lock after ensuring replication is complete or after forcing replication catch-up.
priya: can you paste the commands you'd run? I can run them from my console.
sam: sure — commands I used:
```
# check S3 object etag
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-infra-state-apac --key apac/gpu-pool.tfstate
# pull state locally
terraform state pull > /tmp/gpu-pool.tfstate
# inspect lock item
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name infra-tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "apac/gpu-pool"}}'
# delete lock if confirmed
aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name infra-tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "apac/gpu-pool"}}'
```
marta: also note: if S3 replication is still pending we might remove item and then have the primary and replicated state diverge. maybe safer to run `terraform refresh` locally first and then do a `state push` to reconcile?
alex: good point. alternative safer flow: 1) `terraform state pull` from primary, 2) `terraform state push` to the apac backend (force overwrite) while holding a maintenance window, 3) then remove dynamo lock and re-run apply. That will re-sync replicas quickly. downside: pushes are scary for live infra.
priya: what's our SLA for apac GPU pool? Customer teams already noticed degraded throughput earlier. we need a quick resolution but low-risk.
sam: for quickest low-risk approach: schedule a 15m maintenance window, pause autoscaler, push reconciled state to apac backend, delete orphan lock, then run `terraform plan` and `apply` with us watching nodes join. I'll be oncall and can roll back ASG changes manually if needed.
alex: I've opened a short maintenance window and flipped the CI flag. @marta can you coordinate with capacity owners and post the maintenance in #incidents?
marta: posting now. I'll also notify the cost team because if we accidentally create extra GPUs their chargebacks will spike.
terraform-bot: FYI we've got an open issue with provider 1.8: lock key format changed from `LockID` to `LockKey` which breaks our cleanup script. Filed infra#425.
priya: ok let's do the planned flow. sam/marta/ alex — confirm owners for each step so we don't overlap.
sam: I'll do the state pull/push and lock deletion. alex you monitor apply and ASG. marta handle comms. priya you watch billing alerts.
alex: agreed. I'll also add a pre-apply check to CI that verifies replica etag equality before allowing apply to start — patching the GH Action now.
priya: thanks. after we recover, we should add an automated lock reconciler that understands both key formats and a faster replication check in our preflight. low effort, high ROI. :+1:
marta: noted. will add a ticket to triage and link incident notes.
ci-bot: Maintenance window started by alex at 1992023620 — CI applies to apac disabled.
terraform-bot: Lock removed by sam at 1992023705 (manual delete).
sam: state pushed to apac backend and verified etags match. starting plan now.
alex: plan looks clean, applying in 3..2..
priya: monitors green, nodes are registering, no double-provision. great job everyone. :tada:
marta: follow-up tasks: 1) patch cleanup script for provider key formats, 2) CI preflight replicate check, 3) run a DR test for cross-account state replication in staging. I'll create cards.
alex: thanks all. closing thread once follow-up cards exist.
terraform-bot: Incident note created: infra-2026-03-apac-tfstate-orphan-lock.
